There are a few shortcomings with Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. The main one being the lack of legendary loot. I play these games for the thrill of seeing a legendary item drop and having the icon pop up on the map. In my 20 hours of beating the game, only TWO legendary items dropped before the final fight. I received two more from quests but still, only TWO legendary items dropping in 20 hours of game play is unacceptable. You can argue that this makes greens/blues/purples more balanced but I don't like having to sift through hundreds of weapons to find the right one. When I saw the trailer for this game and the dice rolls I thought they had so much potential to drop good loot but they feel so underwhelming. The loot is easily the biggest problem with the game but everything else is amazing. 

Another shortcoming is the credits. Why are there 20+ minutes of FORCED credits? I'm all for appreciating the developers for the game but when I'm having to sit there for 20-30 minutes and I can't get out that feels real bad. Other reviews mentioned LBGQT being forced down their throats during the game but I didn't notice it (probably because I didn't play with sound for most of it). There's some characters here and there that are LBGQT but overall it doesn't feel pushy. 

In conclusion, this game was a lot of fun for what it is - a Borderlands game mixed in a fantasy world. The story and side quests are at their best but the loot feeling so underwhelming is a clear issue. Also, the credits... WHY

Final Score: 8/10
-1.5 for lackluster loot
-0.5 for 20+ minutes of forced credits

Genuinely the best entry in the series since BL2. Taking the Borderlands formula and planting it in a fantasy world gives so many opportunities to get big and creative with level and enemy design. The mushroom baddies had me shooting inanimate objects, the undead enemies (this game's version of psychos) make you pay more attention to health colours, and the beanstock level is so cool to run around in. There's just a lot of very cool ideas at play here. 

For my money, the Tina DLC from BL2 is the high point of the series, and this game does not hit the emotional high or the originality of that expansion. This game is actually a prequel to that DLC, and I think the storytelling here would have been better served by revealing that much earlier. The writing in Wonderlands in just as annoying as every other post-BL2 game in the franchise, but that is offset by having the most interesting big bad since Handsome Jack. The Dragon Lord is funny, and his storyline is meta in a weird way that I really liked. Will Arnett is a very welcome presense here, he's great, and Ashly Burch is always charming as Tina. Andy Samberg and Wanda Sykes are exciting to hear, but used terribly. Their characters only exist as disembodied voices commenting on your actions, and I think they would work a lot better if they were playing NPCs in the world. That, or just go full meta and have them playing themselves, so they're not confined to their character's archetype. 

The classes are really good, there are a lot of really fun powers. I love the magic system! As a Borderlands player who never remembers to use grenades, magic is so much more interesting and useful in that slot. The only time I've really used grenades frequently in these games is after getting magic missiles in the Tina BL2 DLC, and they've done a good job expanding that system. I mainly played a spellshot, and messed around with different spells. Late-game I barely had to shoot my guns, which was really fun. I also went through the game a second time with a melee focused build, which is tough in the early game, but becomes very doable around midgame when you can balance your attacks and action skills to keep your rage up consistently. I rebound my melee and action to M1 and M2, and I had a blast.

Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is one of those games where you can just tell that every single part of development not only enjoyed what they were working on, but put a ton of love into it as-well. Every Single part of the world feels fleshed out and just right.

Would recommend to anyone that likes Borderlands or Looter Shooters. Especially Those looking to get into the franchise and genre alike.

Voice Acting is also on point.

I was into it at the start, but man… it really fell off. The humour didn’t land for me, and the whole thing started feeling stale and bland pretty fast. Gameplay’s solid enough, but overall it was a total miss. Just didn’t click.

An interesting spin-off of the Borderlands games that brings some new stuff, but is also unfortunately hindered by other aspects.

Based on Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep (originally a BL2 DLC but later released as a standalone), Wonderlands is a new tale being told by Tiny Tina during a game of Bunkers & Badasses, with a new group this time, and the player's character is a newbie in the group.

This time, instead of playing as pre-set characters as in previous Borderlands games, for the first time, the player is able to create their own character, not only choosing how they look and sound but also assigning attribute points as well. While I think the way attributes affect the character feels a little too simple in this game and could have been expanded on, I think this is a good starting point if future Borderlands games (or at least future Wonderlands games) use this concept - which I think they should.

As for designing the character in terms of visuals... While I like the idea, I'm not a fan of the execution. It kinda feels like no matter how much you change your character, they never look satisfying, there is always something off about how they look.

Gameplay-wise, there aren't a lot of complaints - it's basically how other Borderlands games work with a few changes, mostly on how grenades are replaced with spells and how the game now has actual melee combat. While melee combat is very simple and it's really only about holding the middle mouse button to attack, it's still a step in the right direction for future games and far better than other games where it was only guns granting melee damage bonuses and with enemies' melee attacks causing constant knockback. Spells are also a cool addition to the game, working on cooldown (varying with each spell) rather than based on amount and with different effects that go beyond just causing damage, as some spells are more focused on utility. Guns are still mostly guns, with some crossbows and other ranged weapons added to it, but the gunplay is still the same for the most part.

The story is... Okay. I don't hate it, but I don't love it either and I think it's definitely a step back from Assault on Dragon Keep, which was a lot more interesting. The story has its moments, but the villain feels severely underused - it's only later in the game when the villain finally makes an appearance and gives the player's character an actual reason to want to defeat them, before that it's only some lines of dialogue from him and Tina telling the player's character that he's the big bad guy. And after that, the only moment when the villain becomes relevant again besides the occasional dialogue is right close to the end.

Like Borderlands 3 before, Wonderlands has challenges to be completed in each map which involve finding certain things. This is mostly fun and encourages exploration, but the problem is how the game deals with the Loot Die. Basically, without finding these, the chances for higher rarity drops in the game is very low, so finding these die becomes sort of mandatory if the player wants to have a decent chance at acquiring better loot. Fortunately, it only has to be done once, as it carries over to other characters.

The game also removes the ability to farm bosses for drops, as bosses no longer respawn after they're defeated, which is a very weird design choice for a Borderlands spin-off game.

Classes are fun to play as - while the skill selection for each class feels slightly limited, the ability to multi-class later in the game allows for different skills from two different classes to be mixed together, which then allow for some interesting builds.

I also specially like how Myth Ranks work in the game, where points spent are cycled through 4 different groups of stats instead of offering random selections - even though each point has to be spent on each of these different groups, you can choose in which stat inside that group that point goes to, so it's possible to focus and max out certain stats to the player's preferences.

The way the game deals with end-game content is interesting, but extremely repetitive, with the inclusion of Chaos Chambers, a sort of roguelike mode where the player goes into these chambers, getting progressively harder while also unlocking bonuses for the player's character, then rewarding them with loot at the end. It's the main way the game has of acquiring legendaries and it's fun at first, but with a total of 50 chaos levels to progress through, it gets very repetitive very fast.

Overall, Wonderlands does some things right and some things wrong, tries a few new things, some of these work and some don't. There is room for improvement in future games and I hope that some of the new things included in Wonderlands carry over to future games, while others should be improved on.

Gearbox has its up and downs. I hate them for Aliens Colonial Marines and Duke Nukem Forever but I also know they are not a one-time hit title studio (for the most people it must be BL2 as far as I am concerned). Before Borderlands, there was Brother in Arms. And even before that, there were those HL spin-offs. So, Gearbox was doing just fine and somehow reinvented itself again and again. They made themselves popular again and again and I do not think -especially BL2's- this franchise's success is just a coincidence. However, I have played BL3 just recently, and coming to this from there is an obnoxious experience. They rely on the popularity of the BL franchise enough to create spinoffs and release atrocious dlcs at 10$ each. They rely on this damned franchise enough to release two seperate season passes for BL3 and one of them is entirely empty. See where I am getting to? They are able to do stuff or the worst case scenario (in this case it must be Battleborn lmfao) they try different things -mostly what is popular on the market at that time-. But when they figure out it's working and actually working in a magnificient way, they milk the franchise 'til it's dead. Without reinventing and upgrading it of course. The Pre-Sequel also suffered from their stubborness to milk the franchise despite it had good ideas.

I get this is a game from the pandemic era. It is fine. Its scope is not that big, that is why I would like it as a fucking expansion. Or at least launch it at 40 USD and trim down the game if needed because I can assure you much of the game is completely unnecessary and they are just there to boost the length of a walkthrough quite artificially. Endgame is weak compared to other Borderlands entries and DLCs are weaker than any other Borderlands entries. I'll give the credits where it's due. Tiny Tina has its own uniqueness and luckily compared to BL3 it does not host huge-ass empty worlds where you need to drive or run for minutes. It has more concentrated worlds but they are still empty content-wise. They are creative just in art design when it comes to gameplay, there is still nothing. Borderlands or Wonderlands, I know for a fact, needs a better level design and they cannot figure it out for ages. The same complaint goes to a variety of mission designs in the exact same way. The guns are unfortunately pretty much got reskinned over from BL3. There are fun weps but they are mostly bland with the most unique weapons being at endgame again. There are spells instead of bombs where you can zap enemies like Zeus or snap enemies or even shower a meteor on them like Thanos. But in the end, spells are reskinned bombs in general. There are enough classes and you can choose a secondary class (and change it anytime at the endgame), there are enough fun skills so I have no complaint there, you'll have your classic perk tree. 

There are actually new things and they are ok contextually although not big enough to save the whole game. There is an overworld and it's perfectly fine given this is a DnD setting. There are random encounters that await you when exploring the overworld. I do not think they are that hard or long to irritate you but they are just unnecessary. I often think of random encounters as an old-fashioned concept, I know some people like them or do not mind them but if it is not an old jrpg, I would wish there would be better options to farm exp and gear, and guess what? There are. This is a looter shoter. So, even if I can justify the existence of random encounters contextually due to the given setting they are just meh. Enemy types and environments often repeat themselves. 

The story is there with all its references and puns and quibbles, some of them are really genuine but most of them are cringey enough to make you want to rip your ears out. The whole story is simple but adorable enough for a spin-off. Breaks the 4th wall often to make pun of DnD campaigns. After all, the villain itself is a pun to it. Even though he is a parody character he is thousand times better than the jackasses in BL3. Not to mention he has a cool final boss fight (probably the 2nd best next to Handsome Jack). Visually chaotic and satisfying as well as it has enough mechanics for an endgame fight. 
The cast is weak. Except for Tina and gorgeous Butt Stallion and for a brief time Torgue and Brick (with his fairy wings) there is no one. I get the writer team from BL2 may have been long gone but characters stand still and you can still work them out. I do not get why would not apply those characters to this setting. Without a strong cast, it's an even more forgettable experience.

Long story short, there is much more to talk about Gearbox, their pricing policies and the direction where BL goes to. But I believe, this should be enough to give at least an insight about the game, anything more than this would be a BL3 or even a BL franchise criticsm in general than just complaints about Wonderlands. Beatiful setting, terrible execution. I did not expect this game to be a needle mover in fps genre nor reinvent the BL formula but I just can't bear it anymore, especially right after coming from BL3. Do not repeat my mistake if you do not enjoy this franchise anymore. BL needs much more than this and I do not think critics voice it enough to suppress Gearbox. For how long can you enjoy the same formula and how far can you push yourself into giving 8s and 9s to a reskinned game?

To finish my review, I'll quote from another review ''The best and worst thing about Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands is that it feels like another Borderlands game.'' It is entirely true and only bound to your expectations from and perceptions of the game. I hope you enjoy it more where I couldn't even if I am pushed myself hard to.

72/100
